about.name: Kevin Stev Bayer
bio_paragraphs: I'm a Mechatronics Engineering student at KCG College of Technology, Chennai, building intelligent machines at the intersection of software, electronics, and mechanical design. My focus is on autonomous robotics, simulation-driven development, and real-time embedded control — skills I'm actively refining for graduate-level research and industry.

Currently targeting Master's programs in Robotics and Autonomous Systems at TU Munich, ETH Zürich, and KTH Royal Institute of Technology. My portfolio demonstrates hands-on competency in full-stack robotics: from URDF modelling and physics simulation to embedded C++ and ROS2 navigation stacks.

projects.title: Humanoid Robotics Simulation
projects.short_description: Full-body humanoid locomotion in MuJoCo + ROS2, using model-predictive control for dynamic balancing on uneven terrain.
projects.full_description: Designed and simulated a 22-DOF humanoid robot model (URDF + xacro) in MuJoCo 3.x, integrated with ROS2 Humble via mujoco_ros. Implemented a centroidal Model Predictive Controller (MPC) in C++ for real-time dynamic balancing. The simulation covers walking on flat ground and uneven terrain, with full joint-space trajectory planning.
highlights: 22-DOF URDF model built from scratch in SolidWorks, exported to MJCF
C++ MPC controller running at 500 Hz on simulated hardware clock
ROS2 integration: joint state publisher, foot-contact sensor topics, tf2 broadcast
Terrain randomisation scripts in Python for sim-to-real robustness testing

media.image_alt: Humanoid simulation in MuJoCo with ROS2

projects.title: 4WD Tug-of-War Robot
projects.short_description: High-torque 4WD competition robot with custom aluminium chassis, dual L298N drivers, and a traction-optimised PID controller.
projects.full_description: Built for the inter-college tug-of-war competition. Designed a welded aluminium box-section chassis in SolidWorks, 3D-printed motor mounts, and wired dual L298N H-bridge modules for four 300 RPM DC gearbox motors. Wrote a traction-control PID in Arduino C++ that reads wheel-encoder feedback to prevent slip under maximum-torque conditions.
highlights: Custom welded aluminium chassis — 2.4 kg total weight, ~180 N peak traction
Dual L298N H-bridge driver board with PWM speed control
Encoder-based PID traction control prevents wheel spin under load

projects.title: Industrial Robotics — KUKA Internship
projects.short_description: Planned internship project: offline programming and collision-free path planning for KUKA KR10 R1100 arm using KRL and RoboDK.
projects.full_description: Upcoming internship project focused on industrial manipulator programming. Plan includes: offline path generation in RoboDK, KRL (KUKA Robot Language) scripting for pick-and-place and weld seam tracking, digital twin verification in simulation before deploying to physical hardware. Will document the full workflow from CAD import to real robot execution.
highlights: KUKA KR10 R1100 — 6-DOF, 10 kg payload industrial arm
Offline programming workflow: RoboDK → KRL → KUKA KRC4 controller
Planned collision-free path planning using OMPL integration
Digital twin verification loop before physical deployment

projects.title: Autonomous Line-Following Robot
projects.short_description: IR-sensor-based differential-drive robot with tuned PID controller and secondary obstacle-avoidance behaviour layer.
projects.full_description: Built a differential-drive robot with an 8-channel IR sensor array for line detection. Implemented a cascaded PID controller in Python for smooth trajectory tracking. Added ultrasonic obstacle avoidance as a finite-state-machine layer on top of the line-follow controller. First competition entry — achieved 2nd place finish.
highlights: Sub-5 mm path deviation with well-tuned PID gains (Kp=1.8, Ki=0.02, Kd=0.9)
8-channel TCRT5000 IR array, sampled at 100 Hz via Arduino interrupt

projects.title: ROS2 Sensor Fusion Node
projects.short_description: Custom ROS2 node fusing LIDAR and IMU data for real-time 2D occupancy mapping, visualised in rviz2.
projects.full_description: Developed a custom ROS2 (Humble) node that subscribes to LIDAR (RPLidar A1) and IMU (MPU6050) topics, applies a complementary filter for orientation estimation, and publishes a fused pose estimate with a 2D occupancy grid. Visualised in rviz2 with live tf2 transforms.
highlights: Pub/sub architecture with tf2 broadcast — map → odom → base_link
Complementary filter (α=0.98) for IMU noise reduction
Real-time 2D occupancy grid at 5 Hz published to /map
